criteria.no: No: the item is silent or only topical about panics, or some waiting caller gets no error.
criteria.unclear: Whether every waiting caller gets an error cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: Yes: every waiting caller gets an error after a writer panic.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` say that a SQLite writer-thread panic results in an error for every caller waiting on it? Judge presence only.

criteria.no: No such outcome is stated, including when the item is silent about panics.
criteria.unclear: It may leave a waiting caller hanging but cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: Some waiting caller is stated or plainly described to wait indefinitely after a writer panic.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` leave any caller waiting on the SQLite writer thread without an error after the writer panics (for example replies never sent, or queued requests left pending)? Silence about panics is not conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item concerns something other than the SQLite writer thread, such as unrelated documentation, CI, release work, or another database's components.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell whether it touches the SQLite writer thread, its request channel or its reply path.
criteria.yes: The item creates, configures or changes the SQLite writer thread, the channel callers use to send it requests, or the way replies or errors reach those callers.

relevant.instructions: Does the work described in `item.text` implement or change the SQLite writer thread, its request channel, or its reply path (the area named in `anchor.scope`)? Judge subject overlap only; do not judge whether the item follows `anchor.statement`.
